findings.F1: American IPA ˈɪ.rɑn is wrong (should be ˈaɪ.ɚn) and contradicts the EYE-ern respelling.
findings.F2: Sense 1 example states a checkable science fact (melting point of iron).
findings.F3: Definition of 'strike while the iron is hot' says wait until calm, the opposite of act while the chance lasts.
findings.F4: see_also repeats iron-v (word family) and steel-n (compare).
findings.F5: The common informal idiom 'pump iron' has no phrase.
findings.F6: Pronunciation adaptation note restates the pronunciation note and says the American r comes at the end.
findings.F7: Pronunciation note's sentence about where the r is said is vague and wrong for both varieties.
